facts.fact: The S&P 500 fell about 48% from January 11, 1973 to October 3, 1974.
The S&P 500 did not regain its January 1973 high until July 1980, roughly 7.5 years after the peak (price only, before dividends).
Headline CPI inflation peaked at 14.8% in March 1980.
The federal funds rate reached a record 20% in late 1980.
Unemployment peaked at 10.8% in late 1982.
Inflation fell to 3.7% in 1983.
The 30-year fixed mortgage rate peaked at 18.63% in October 1981.
The S&P 500 fell about 33.5% from August 25, 1987 to December 4, 1987.
The S&P 500 regained its prior high on July 26, 1989, about 23 months after the peak.
The Nasdaq Composite peaked at 5,048.62 on March 10, 2000.
By October 2002 the Nasdaq had fallen about 78% from its peak.
The S&P 500 fell about 49% from March 24, 2000 to October 9, 2002, and regained that high in May 2007.
About $5 trillion in stock market value was lost from the peak to the end of the 2002 downturn.
The S&P 500 fell about 57% from October 9, 2007 to March 9, 2009, and regained its prior closing high in March 2013.
U.S. home prices fell about 34% from their July 2006 peak by early 2012 (S&P/Case-Shiller).
The S&P 500 fell about 34% from February 19, 2020 to March 23, 2020.
The S&P 500 closed at a new record high on August 18, 2020, about five months after the low.
CPI rose 9.1% over the 12 months ending June 2022, the largest increase since November 1981.
Over the same 12 months, food prices rose 10.4% and energy prices rose 41.6%.
The S&P 500 fell about 25% from January 3, 2022 to October 12, 2022, and regained its prior high in January 2024.
